correctness.rationale: For every part \(V_i\), all vertices have exactly \(s-s_i\) neighbors in the selected set. An omitted vertex in that part has exactly \(N-s-n_i+s_i\) neighbors in the omitted set. Therefore the two stated inequalities are exactly equivalent to the definition, including the vacuous restrained condition on a fully selected part. The enumerator follows by translating these inequalities into the exact coordinate range for each part and multiplying binomial choice counts. Brute-force replay through order 9 matched the criterion and every coefficient.

value.rationale: The result is not merely another scalar bound: it classifies every feasible selected-set profile for arbitrary part sizes and every admissible k, and packages those profiles into an exact cardinality enumerator. The minimum parameter, the number of optimum solutions, and every higher-cardinality count are all recoverable. This is a natural strengthening of prior complete-multipartite minimum bounds and is structurally useful because the precise partwise failure mechanisms are explicit.
